sources.citation: De Wolf AM, Van Zundert TC, De Cooman S, Hendrickx JF. Theoretical effect of hyperventilation on speed of recovery and risk of rehypnotization following recovery - a Gas Man simulation. BMC Anesthesiology. 2012;12:22.
sources.note: Tier 3, reference implementation (see docs/MODEL.md, 'Source hierarchy'). Table 1 reports the Gas Man desflurane blood:gas and tissue:gas coefficients used here, in the same table already cited for sevoflurane. De Wolf et al. ran Gas Man simulations and measured no coefficient: Table 1 is the parameter set they supplied to it, so this is the Gas Man set carrying a journal's name rather than a measurement. It is the source of the stored values.

sources.citation: Eger EI II. Partition coefficients of I-653 in human blood, saline, and olive oil. Anesthesia & Analgesia. 1987;66(10):971-973.
sources.note: Tier 1, primary measurement, cited but not adopted. Human study reporting a blood:gas coefficient of 0.424 +/- 0.024 (mean +/- SD) at 37 degrees C in 11 ASA I-III patients aged 25-76, for I-653 (desflurane's development code name). The stored value 0.42 is the Gas Man figure and is 0.9 percent lower - the closest agreement of the three agents. PL-D6LX carries the decision.

sources.citation: Yasuda N, Targ AG, Eger EI II. Solubility of I-653, sevoflurane, isoflurane, and halothane in human tissues. Anesthesia & Analgesia. 1989;69(3):370-373.
sources.note: Tier 1, primary measurement, cited but not adopted. Human tissue study reporting an I-653 (desflurane) brain:blood partition coefficient of 1.29 +/- 0.05 at 37 degrees C. The stored tissue:gas values are Gas Man's; dividing vessel_rich by blood:gas gives an implied brain:blood of 0.54/0.42 = 1.286, 0.3 percent below Yasuda's measurement. Same paper already cited for sevoflurane's and isoflurane's tissue-solubility models, where the group-weighting obstacle to adopting it is recorded.

sources.citation: Johnston RV, Andrews JJ, Deyo DJ, Trahan LA, Savrick MD, Grady JJ, Prough DS. The effects of carrier gas composition on the performance of the Tec 6 desflurane vaporizer. Anesthesia & Analgesia. 1994;79(3):548-552.
sources.note: Primary source for a device capability: docs/MODEL.md's source hierarchy concerns measured physiologic quantities, and a calibrated dial maximum is not one. Tec 6 vaporizer output was analyzed at all integer dial settings from 1% to 18%, confirming 18% as the device's calibrated maximum. Used here as max_delivered_concentration_percent. This is a device-capability limit on the delivered-concentration control, not a scientific model parameter; it does not affect the governing equations.

sources.citation: Nickalls RWD, Mapleson WW. Age-related iso-MAC charts for isoflurane, sevoflurane and desflurane in man. British Journal of Anaesthesia. 2003;91(2):170-174.
sources.note: The stored mac_percent is tier 3: it is the flat adult MAC De Wolf et al. state they used in their Gas Man simulations, not a value taken from this paper. Nickalls and Mapleson is the tier 1 age-related source, cited but not adopted, because MAC is age-dependent and this project's reference-adult model has no age parameter, so mac_percent uses the flat adult value from De Wolf et al. above (same paper already cited for partition coefficients: 'MAC values that we used in our Gas Man simulations are: desflurane 6%, sevoflurane 2%, isoflurane 1.2%'), not an age-adjusted one. Used as the controller's starting delivered-concentration default (1 MAC), not a governing-equation parameter.
